subject: AWS Marketplace: evidence collection & SSO provisioning for Fulfillment
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@acme-analytics.com>, DevOps <devops@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS Marketplace: evidence collection & SSO provisioning for Fulfillment

Hi Samantha / Acme team,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. As we discussed, the next two items to unblock AWS Marketplace SaaS Fulfillment are: 1) evidence package for procurement/Security (SOC2, TLS, data residency notes) and 2) SSO provisioning + role mapping so our fulfillment API can call into your entitlement service during activation.

I pulled together a short checklist below — can you confirm who on your side will own each item and share the artifacts by Friday? If timelines are tight we can run a lightweight one-week evidence exchange and retro-fit additional docs during the pilot.

- SOC2 snapshot (latest reporting period) — Procurement/Security
- Proof of TLS + cert chain summary — DevOps
- SSO metadata (IdP metadata XML or SAML metadata URL) + recommended role mappings — DevOps
- API scopes required by Redwood Fulfillment (see attached CSV) — Marissa/Redwood to confirm with Engineering
- Account & billing contact for DocuSign and billing setup — Procurement

Attachments: Fulfillment-API-scopes.csv (CSV stub)

Proposed next steps:
1) DevOps shares SSO metadata and confirms allowed redirect URIs by EOD Thu
2) Procurement sends SOC2 snapshot and billing contact by Fri
3) Redwood will provision a test tenant and run a sample entitlement activation (ETA 48 hours after we get SSO metadata)

Ben / Karthik — looping you in for technical support and SSO validation.

Thanks,

— Marissa

From: Samantha Lee <samantha@acme-analytics.com>

Cc: DevOps <devops@acme-analytics.com>, Procurement <procure@acme-analytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace: evidence collection & SSO provisioning for Fulfillment

Hi Marissa — thanks for the summary. We're aligned on the checklist. A few clarifications from our side before we send artifacts: 

1) SOC2: we can share the SOC2 snapshot but Procurement wants a redacted copy (PII removed). Is that acceptable for Marketplace submission or do you need unredacted for internal legal review?

2) SSO: Our IdP is Okta. We'll export the metadata XML and the signing cert. Can you confirm the attributes Redwood expects (email, groups, role)? Also, do you require a pre-provisioning webhook to seed accounts before first activation?

3) API scopes: the attached CSV looks ok but DevOps wants to confirm that the fulfillment API will only request entitlement:activate and entitlement:query (no user-data reads). Please confirm ASAP.

We'll attach the requested files in a separate email from DevOps. Procurement will send their contact details after a quick legal check.

Best,
Samantha
Head of IT Integrations
Acme Analytics

Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace: evidence collection & SSO provisioning for Fulfillment

Hi all — attaching the IdP metadata and a short SSO config dump. We've also included our recommended role mapping:

- acme:MarketplaceAdmin -> map to redwood:fulfillment_admin
- acme:Engineer -> map to redwood:fulfillment_operator

We do not want pre-provisioning webhooks that create user records in our directory — prefer on-demand provisioning during the first activation event.

Attached: acme_sso_config.json (IdP metadata + cert stub)

Notes for Redwood engineering: the environment we'll point at for the pilot is auth.acme-staging.internal. We'll provide a temporary VPN jump-host for calls from Redwood test env if you need to reach internal endpoints; alternatively, we can stand up an externally reachable SAML assertion consumer URL if you can host test ACS endpoints.

— DevOps (on behalf of Samantha)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@acme-analytics.com>, DevOps <devops@acme-analytics.com>, Procurement <procure@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: AWS Marketplace: evidence collection & SSO provisioning for Fulfillment — mutual action plan

Thanks — this is great, and the IdP metadata looks clean. Quick summary / mutual action plan so we have a single source of truth for the pilot rollout: 

A) What Acme will deliver (by Fri 2026-05-07):
  - Procurement: redacted SOC2 snapshot + billing contact (Procurement <procure@acme-analytics.com>)
  - DevOps: SAML metadata (delivered), allowed ACS URL for the externally reachable test ACS (or confirmation to use VPN jump-host), and final role mapping

B) What Redwood will deliver (ETA after SSO confirmed):
  - Provision test tenant + temporary API key for fulfillment calls (within 24 hours of receiving ACS confirmation)
  - Run entitlement activation smoke test (entitlement:activate + entitlement:query) and share logs with Acme's DevOps (we will redact token values)
  - Provide a short runbook for failure modes (401/403 mapping, clock skew, cert rotation)

C) Compliance notes: Redwood's security team requires an unredacted SOC2 report only if Acme requests Redwood to sign a custom SOC2 addendum; otherwise the redacted snapshot is sufficient for Marketplace listing. We'll accept a redacted copy for now and surface to our legal team for a standard review.

D) Next meeting: Wed 2026-05-06 10:00 AM PT — 30 min technical handoff (Ben + Karthik + Acme DevOps)

Attached for reference: Fulfillment-API-scopes.csv (original), SOC2-snapshot-2025.pdf (placeholder).

Soojin — looping you in for billing/fulfillment contract details and to confirm whether the AWS Marketplace contract template requires any field-level changes for Acme's billing GL references.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the pilot running.
